title: Review: Photosynthesis overview, pigments and chromatography; Light-dependent reactions; Light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle); Oxidative phosphorylation and chemiosmosis; Anaerobic respiration; Link reaction and Krebs cycle; Cell signaling and receptors (general)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RS03a#t1 term and clue written for the game; RS02#t3 term and clue written for the game; RS02#t1 term and clue written for the game; HO08a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: HO08a#N.8, PS01a#N.10, PS02a#N.12b, PS03#N.11b, RS03a#N.5b, RS04#N.3b, HO08a#N.3, PS01a#N.7b, PS02a#N.4b, PS03#N.2b, RS03a#N.3b, HO08a#N.5a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Chemiosmosis
items.clue: Making ATP using energy from a proton gradient.

items.label: Intermembrane space
items.clue: Narrow gap between the outer and inner boundaries of a mitochondrion.

items.label: Cristae
items.clue: Folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane, holding the electron carriers.

items.label: Target cell
items.clue: Carries the specific binding protein for a messenger, so it alone responds.

questions.stem: Vibrio fischeri produces light when packed at high density inside the light organ of a squid, but not when living at low density in seawater. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The squid releases a chemical into its light organ that switches on the light-producing genes of the bacteria living there.
Each bacterium switches on its light-producing genes independently when its supply of nutrients in the light organ is high enough.
Autoinducer secreted by each cell only reaches the threshold that switches on the light-producing genes when cells are dense.
The autoinducer accumulating in the light organ is itself the substance that gives out light when it reaches high concentration.

questions.stem: A student claims that photosynthesis by cyanobacteria, which are prokaryotes, produced the oxygenated atmosphere of early Earth. Which of the following provides the best support for this claim?

options.text: Cyanobacteria release more O₂ each year than all the land plants on Earth do today.
Cyanobacteria are simpler than eukaryotes, so they must have photosynthesized first.
Signs of free O₂ first appear in rocks formed when cyanobacteria existed but no eukaryotes did.
Early organisms needed O₂, so cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis in order to make it.

questions.stem: A chemical is added to illuminated chloroplasts. It makes the thylakoid membrane freely permeable to H⁺ but does not affect the photosystems, the electron transport chain, or ATP synthase. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: More ATP is made, and NADPH is made too.
ATP and NADPH are both made as before.
Neither ATP nor NADPH is made any longer.
Less ATP is made, but NADPH is still made.

questions.explanation: Electron transport from water to NADP⁺ continues, so NADPH is still made. But H⁺ now leaks back across the membrane instead of through ATP synthase, so less ATP is made.

questions.stem: Intact chloroplasts isolated from spinach leaves are kept in bright light in a solution that contains everything they need for photosynthesis. All CO₂ is then removed from the solution while the light stays on. Which prediction about the release of O₂ by the chloroplasts over the next few minutes is best supported?

options.text: It stops at once, as the O₂ released is made from the CO₂ the chloroplasts take in.
It is unchanged, as the light reactions run independently of the Calvin cycle.
It increases, as light energy that the Calvin cycle no longer uses goes to the light reactions.
It decreases, as the Calvin cycle stops returning NADP⁺ to the light reactions.

questions.stem: In aerobic cellular respiration, which process is called oxidative phosphorylation?

options.text: The addition of oxygen atoms from O₂ to ADP, which forms ATP in the mitochondrial matrix
Any ATP synthesis in glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, as carbon atoms of glucose are oxidized
The addition of a phosphate to ADP by each carrier of the ETC as an electron passes through it
ATP synthesis by ATP synthase, powered by H⁺ flowing back across the inner membrane

questions.explanation: ADP + Pᵢ → ATP by ATP synthase, driven by H⁺ flowing back by chemiosmosis down the gradient that electron transport set up.

questions.stem: A mutant strain of a hypothetical yeast species cannot convert pyruvate into ethanol and CO₂. Wild-type and mutant cells are placed in a glucose solution with no O₂. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: Glycolysis soon stops in the mutant but not the wild type, as NAD⁺ is not regenerated from NADH.
Glycolysis continues in the mutant, but it makes less ATP, as the fermentation step makes the ATP.
Glycolysis continues in the mutant, as NADH passes electrons through the ETC to CO₂ instead.
Glycolysis stops in both strains, as glycolysis needs O₂ to oxidize glucose to pyruvate.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a ligand and its receptor?

options.text: The receptor's binding site converts the ligand into a product, in the way an enzyme's active site converts a substrate.
The ligand binds reversibly to a binding site on the receptor protein that is complementary to it, and the receptor changes shape.
Any ligand reaching a cell binds to it, because every cell carries receptors for every signalling chemical in the body.
The ligand passes through a channel in the receptor into the cytoplasm, where it brings about the response directly.

questions.explanation: Binding is reversible and does not alter the ligand; the receptor's change of shape starts the cell's response.

questions.stem: Electron micrographs of chloroplasts show grana. Which statement correctly describes grana?

options.text: They are stacks of thylakoids, the site of the light reactions.
They are stacks of thylakoids, where CO₂ is made into sugar.
They are the fluid around the thylakoids, where the Calvin cycle runs.
They are folds of the inner membrane, where the light reactions happen.

questions.explanation: Thylakoids are organized in stacks called grana, and the light reactions of photosynthesis occur in the grana.

questions.stem: During the light reactions, water molecules are split. What is the role of this process?

options.text: It releases the energy that boosts electrons in photosystem II.
It supplies the oxygen atoms that are built into carbohydrate.
It supplies electrons to replace those lost from photosystem II.
It gives electrons that reduce CO₂ directly to carbohydrate.

questions.explanation: Light boosts electrons in photosystem II, and they leave along the ETC. Splitting water supplies electrons to replace them, releasing O₂ and H⁺.

questions.stem: A student is drawing a model of how the two stages of photosynthesis in a chloroplast are connected. Which set of arrows between the light reactions and the Calvin cycle should the model show?

options.text: ATP and NADPH from the light reactions to the Calvin cycle; no arrow going back to it
ATP and NADPH from the light reactions to the Calvin cycle; ADP, Pᵢ and NADP⁺ back
ATP and NADPH from the Calvin cycle to the light reactions; ADP, Pᵢ and NADP⁺ back again
Absorbed light energy from the light reactions to the Calvin cycle; no arrow going back

questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares the mitochondrial matrix with the intermembrane space while electron transport is taking place?

options.text: The matrix has the lower pH, as the ETC moves H⁺ into the matrix from the intermembrane space.
The matrix has the lower pH, as the ETC moves H⁺ out of the matrix into the intermembrane space.
The matrix has the higher pH, as the ETC moves H⁺ out of the matrix into the intermembrane space.
The two have the same pH, as H⁺ crosses the lipid bilayer freely until it is spread evenly.

questions.stem: At a synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle cell, the neuron releases the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, which causes the muscle cell to contract. Which statement correctly describes how this signal reaches the muscle cell?

options.text: It diffuses across the narrow gap between the neuron and the muscle cell next to it.
It is carried in the blood from the neuron to muscle cells all over the body.
It crosses the gap as an electric current that jumps from the neuron into the muscle cell.
It moves toward the muscle cell, because the muscle cell needs it in order to contract.
